trainers.instruction: Select the image of the underworld.

hint.text: The underworld is recognisable by its ruler, Hades, and his three-headed dog.
hint.sound: The underworld is recognisable by its ruler, Haydeez, and his three-headed dog.

feedback.finish: In Greek mythology, the underworld was the realm that souls would travel to after death.

instruction.text: Place the coin in Charon’s hand to learn more about the journey to the underworld.
instruction.sound: Place the coin in Care-on’s hand to learn more about the journey to the underworld.

atoms.b: The underworld was believed to be surrounded by ((++rivers mountains)). The souls had to ask Charon, the ((++ferryman pilot)), to sail them across.
Dead ancient Greeks were often buried with ((++coins candy)) to pay Charon. Without this fare, souls were doomed to walk the ((++riverbank desert)) for eternity.
According to myth, Cerberus guarded the gates to the ((++underworld insideworld)). His three heads were believed to represent the past, ((++present absent)) and future.
Cerberus stopped the living from entering and the ((++dead living)) from escaping. His ((++terrifying adorable)) appearance helped scare off anyone who dared to approach!

instruction.text: What was Cerberus’s role in the underworld? Select all correct answers.

b: to escort the gods into the underworld

atoms.b: Not everyone in the underworld went to the same place. The ((++greatest worst)) people, like heroes and poets, went to Elysium, a ((++peaceful horrible)) land of music and light!
Ordinary people went to the Fields of Asphodel, a quiet, ((++grey colourful)) place where souls wandered.
The worst people went to Tartarus, a dark place deep underground. Here, souls were ((++punished celebrated)) for their evil actions.

trainers.instruction: Listen and decide which part of the underworld these souls would go to.

atoms.sound: a kind poet who wrote beautiful stories about love and peace
a regular farmer who worked hard and treated others with respect
a cruel king who harmed his people and caused a war
